answer:
Mode collapse occurs when many latent inputs produce only a few outputs, omitting real-data modes. With the original saturating generator loss $\log(1-D(G(z)))$, a discriminator that confidently separates generated data can provide weak gradients through its saturated probability. The common non-saturating generator loss helps this issue but does not eliminate collapse. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.00028) [2](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/)

WGAN uses a real-valued 1-Lipschitz critic to estimate Wasserstein distance, which can supply useful transport-related gradients even for separated supports. WGAN-GP penalizes $(\|\nabla_{\hat x}f(\hat x)\|_2-1)^2$ on interpolated samples to encourage the constraint. This sampled penalty is not a global proof of Lipschitzness, and training still needs optimization and capacity control. Report diversity/coverage and training stability rather than claiming the method universally fixes every GAN failure.
